hits.title: Cortex ops sweep: CPU debug, vectorizer 3.3.0, parquet quarantine
hits.body:
Single Cortex operator session covering 22h on 2026-05-04/05.

## Diagnostico 172% CPU
cortex-api consumindo 50% por archive_loader em loop 30s sobre 104 parquets sem cache mtime, decomprime zstd integral por tick + parquet corrompido em year=2026/month=04/day=28/hour=16 (loga WARN indefinido, sem quarentena automatica). cortex-nexus 100% sem queries 6+min, sem error/warn, busy-loop interno (healthcheck falso-unhealthy por `curl` ausente na imagem).

## Fix aplicado
Quarentena manual do parquet corrompido em /var/lib/cortex/archive/quarantine/raw-00000.parquet.corrupt as 07:29 UTC. Loop WARN parou. Cortex-nexus continua sob investigacao.

## Vectorizer 3.2.0 -> 3.3.0
Issue #265 fechada: endpoint POST /collections/{src}/vectors/move + SDK methods delete_vector / delete_vectors / move_to_collection. Bumps: docker-compose.yml linha 3, Cargo.toml linha 56, Cargo.lock (vectorizer-sdk + vectorizer-protocol). Quality gate: cargo check --workspace PASS, docker pull hivehub/vectorizer:3.3.0 OK, docker compose up -d vectorizer aplicado.

## Saldo da sessao
42 turns substantivos, 669 tool calls, ~33k chars de prosa real. Trabalho cobre debugging de producao + atualizacao de dependencia + documentacao em rulebook. Conteudo digno de consolidacao permanente.

- archive_loader precisa cache mtime + quarentena automatica de parquets corrompidos
- healthchecks docker baseados em `curl` falham silenciosamente quando o binario nao existe na imagem
- vectorizer 3.3.0 ja oferece move_to_collection nativo (era hack via reqwest antes)

hits.title: Cortex rework analysis: 4 agents diagnose 80% structural debt, propose 7 ADRs an
hits.body:
Operator-mandated review of Cortex implementation after frustration: consolidation does not work, memory cleanup requires brute force, retrieved data has no relevance. Five-file analysis in `docs/analysis/rework/` (1142 lines) produced by 4 agents in parallel (3 researchers + 1 architect).

## Diagnosis
**80% structural debt / 20% upstream patches.** Stack itself (Synap/Vectorizer/Nexus/Meili/SQLite) is correct; the plumbing between them is ad-hoc.

## Top defects identified
- **Consolidator silent in prod**: no nightly daemon, only manual CLI. `publish_consolidation()` posts to `localhost:17010` which is not reachable from inside the container — every envelope drops.
- **Memory cleanup brute force**: archive Parquet only has per-event delete via `/v1/admin/forget` (no cron sweep). CAS vacuum silent-fails behind a 50% safeguard. Tool-call digest is opt-in.
- **Relevance death**: queries without `scope.repo` fall to `cortex-unknown-*` (zero hits). 2 of 3 repos have empty Meili indexes. Graph topology flat (2 of ~12 edge types in use).
- **Common root**: 6 retention gaps + consolidator gap are all the same shape — missing `Sweep` trait, missing `EnvelopeProducer` trait, missing typed `Lane`, missing `EventIdentity`.

## Recommendation
Medium rework — Phase A (10d, codify traits, no new feature), Phase B (10d, rewrite consolidator/pruner/dashboard on top of traits), Phase C (10d, multi-repo + golden-set eval). Phase A is a mandatory gate. 7 ADRs (009-015) drafted with explicit trade-offs.

- Cortex stack choice is defensible; the inter-module plumbing is the regret
- Six retention bugs share one shape: no Sweep trait — that is the load-bearing fix
- Consolidator never ran in prod because publish target was unreachable inside the container
- Relevance failures trace to missing scope.repo defaults + empty per-repo Meili indexes

hits.title: Refactor two 5K-line files into submodules + fix retention pipeline end-to-end
hits.body:
Split `cortex-api/src/dashboard.rs` (5005→415 lines, 17 submodules) and `cortex-cli/src/bin/cortex-ops.rs` (4962→1131 lines, 16 submodules) for maintainability. Reorganized 32 operator scripts into thematic subdirectories (sweeps, doctor, graph, probes, setup).

Fixed retention pipeline: implemented missing `turn_digest_live.rs` backend, corrected consolidator nightly to run at topic granularity, resolved CORTEX_HOME fallback chain in metadata-DB lookups, fixed digest envelope schema validation (missing context/decision fields), added Vectorizer JWT auth for `/v1/admin/forget`, recovered ULID timestamps when archive_loader stamps `ts=0`, and handled partial zstd frames in archive purge. Validated end-to-end: digests enumerate real events, persist with correct schema, and purge old tool_call/turn records.

16 commits landed (refactor + 8 bug fixes). All quality gates passing. Handoff at context limit with retention drains in background.

- Large monolithic files (>4000 LOC) fragment into per-topic submodules reliably: 17-submodule dashboard split reduced parent by 75% while improving IDE navigation and test isolation.
- Retention pipeline is multi-subsystem (tool_call_digest, turn_digest, memory_consolidate, archive_purge); silent cron failures occur when any backend is misconfigured or missing—test enumerator + persister + purger as one integration, not separately.
- Environment variable fallback chains (CORTEX_HOME → ~/.cortex → /var/lib/cortex) must be consistent across all CLI subcommands in container deployments; cortex-ops schedule list/run-now silently used wrong DB when CORTEX_HOME was unset in docker-compose.

hits.title: Cortex daemon recovery + memory cleanup (graph analysis, phase11v, phase11w)
hits.body:
Started with codebase exploration to understand Cortex's data model, then shifted to operational debugging when user reported retention daemon broken. Discovered six independent gaps (hardcoded dashboard, unresolved env vars, missing cron seeds, cron wraparound bug, missing schema, missing bookkeeping) and implemented phase11v (`crates/cortex-api/src/dashboard.rs`, `crates/cortex-workers/src/retention/scheduler.rs`, `crates/cortex-storage/src/metadata.rs`, `crates/cortex-cli/src/bin/cortex-ops.rs` bookkeeping injection). Simultaneously built phase11w tool-call digest summarizer (`crates/cortex-workers/src/retention/tool_call_digest.rs`, `crates/cortex-api/src/admin_list_events.rs`) as a weekly cron job to purge old tool-call events from Meili and reduce memory bloat.

Early in session, created `scripts/graph_correlate.py` and `scripts/cypher_load.py` to materialize cross-project graph; load attempt to Nexus hit timeout/panic issues (17+ repos, 400k+ Cypher statements). Did not debug the Nexus issue further—focus shifted to live retention failures.

All tests pass. Containers rebuilt and deployed live. Retention sweeps now fire on cron, memory now has a purge path via tool-call digest.

- Dashboard retention_state was hardcoded to 'never' (line 3639–3653 `crates/cortex-api/src/dashboard.rs`). Must read live from `metadata.sqlite cron_jobs` table, not compute in test-mode logic. This masked all upstream issues.
- Retention daemon cron seed was idempotent-broken: used `INSERT OR IGNORE` instead of `INSERT OR REPLACE`, so first boot's defaults locked in forever. Next attempt at `seed_defaults` became a no-op. Fixed via explicit UPSERT in `scheduler.rs` and dashboard live-read flow.
- Tool-call digest (phase11w) mirrors turn_digest pattern: buckets by `(ts_week, repo, symbol)`, summarises 50+ calls into 1 memory row, purges originals via `/v1/admin/forget`. New endpoint `/v1/admin/list-events?kind=tool_call&before=<ts>&limit=N` powers the enumerator (`tool_call_digest_live.rs` fetches, summarizes, persists, forgets in one sweep).

hits.title: HiveLLM ecosystem consolidation: 18 projects → standardized knowledge base
hits.body:
Session synthesized every HiveLLM repository (Cortex, Vectorizer, Nexus, Synap, Lexum, Rulebook, Expert, Tml, Umicp, HiveGPU, Transmutation, TransmutationLite, TmlDocs, TmlTextmate, Assets, CompressionPrompt, HivehubCloud, VectorizerSync) into a structured per-project knowledge base at `docs/consolidation/<Project>/` using a standardized 9-section template: overview, architecture, public APIs/surface, data & storage, integrations, design decisions & rationale, operations, Cortex relevance, and open questions—166 markdown files total.

Workflow: directory discovery → parallel research agents per project (using Agent tool) → markdown synthesis per standard template → single commit `7f1b7fb`. Key ecosystem topology discovered: Cortex is the cognitive hub that ingests metadata from {Vectorizer for embeddings, Nexus for graph persistence, Synap for event distribution, Lexum as search alternative, Expert for specialized reasoning, HiveGPU for optional GPU acceleration}. TML is the substrate language; Rulebook standardizes AI development practices. All open questions, architectural gaps, and integration unknowns were explicitly catalogued in section 09 of each project for Cortex's future consolidation phases.

- Standardized template (sections 01–09 + README per project) enables consistent knowledge ingestion into Cortex without manual rewrite—pattern: identify → synthesize into fixed sections → Cortex-relevance bridge (§08) → gaps & unknowns (§09).
- Cross-project dependency graph is now explicit in the '05-integrations' and '08-cortex-relevance' files per project: Cortex is explicitly mapped as consuming Vectorizer (embeddings), Nexus (graph), Synap (events), Expert (reasoning)—integration roadmap for phase13c onwards.
- Systematic open-questions documentation (section 09 per project) surfaces unresolved design items (Vectorizer upsert semantics, Synap cluster-mode timeline, Lexum distributed consensus, TmlDocs package registry scope) and architectural unknowns—feeds Cortex's research priorities and task dependencies.

hits.title: Independent second-opinion analysis of Cortex rework strategy
hits.body:
Session audited Cortex's consolidator/pruner/retention/API/MCP stack against prior 4-doc rework analysis. Performed systematic code exploration across key boundaries: consolidator binary entry point (cortex-consolidator.rs), pruner daemon (pruner/engine.rs), retention logic (turn_digest, tool_call_digest, cas_vacuum), API handlers (admin_forget, ingest_proxy, dashboard/consolidations), and MCP server integration. Spawned two Agent passes: one to identify blind spots beyond prior analysis, one to validate which prior findings remain open vs already fixed.

Synthesized independent second-opinion analysis (opus5.7/) with three documents: validation delta (reconciling prior 01-consolidation/02-memory-cleanup/03-relevance/04-architecture findings against current code), blind spots (gaps in prior analysis scope), and strategic recommendation (feature freeze + Phase A++ + 4-week checkpoint). Both minmax2.7 and opus5.7 analyses converged on "medium-rework" assessment of the stack. Committed 8 files (1967 insertions) in hash e363ba5, adding `docs/analysis/rework/opus5.7/` and `docs/analysis/rework/minmax2.7/` to repository.

- Systematic code audit at multiple abstraction levels (daemon loop → API handler → persistence layer) before committing to rework strategy. Session traced consolidator.rs entry point → pruner/engine.rs daemon loop → retention/*.rs drop logic → API handlers (admin_forget.rs, dashboard/consolidations.rs) → MCP integration, catching edge cases that high-level analysis alone misses.
- Convergent multi-perspective analysis reduces rework risk: two independent analyses (minmax2.7, opus5.7) agreed on "medium-rework" strategy, validating the approach; single-perspective analysis would lack this validation signal.
- Analysis-first discipline before task creation: synthesize findings and strategy in docs/analysis/ before creating .rulebook/tasks/ or spawning implementers. Project rule `consult-analysis-before-implementing.md` expects this pattern and reduces rework cycles.

hits.title: Graph explorer filtering by project + cross-project correlation view
hits.body:
User requested graph explorer scoped per project with cross-project correlation. Agent extracted `RepoMultiSelect` atom from Timeline (shared picker) and integrated it into Graph.tsx, adding three loader modes: panorama (institutional nodes only), drilldown (single-repo detail), and correlation (multi-repo patterns). 

Initial implementation had case-sensitivity issues with repo name matching, surfaced in turn 3. Root cause discovered in turn 5: Nexus graph schema only persists `Artifact -[:IN_REPO]-> Repo` relationships; `Decision` and `Analysis` nodes have no `IN_REPO` edges. This meant the panorama was collapsing incorrectly when trying to correlate repos. Rewrote graph filtering logic to handle this schema reality — panorama now displays only core institutional nodes (Repo, Decision, Law, Analysis); sessions/turns/memories enter only via drilldown or cross-repo traversal.

**Files**: `gui/src/atoms/RepoMultiSelect.tsx` (new, extracted); `gui/src/views/Graph.tsx` (mode-aware filtering); `gui/src/views/Timeline.tsx` (import update); `crates/cortex-api/src/dashboard/graph.rs` (schema reference). Typecheck + 31/31 tests green at session end.

- Nexus schema limitation: only `Artifact -[:IN_REPO]-> Repo` persists; Decision and Analysis nodes lack IN_REPO edges. Panorama filtering must account for this asymmetry (confirmed turn 5, `01KQV7YRZDRM2S7C4321V0EPDJ`).
- Extracted `RepoMultiSelect` as shared atom for reuse across Graph and Timeline views (turns 1–2, `01KQV74ABT257552ZZ25RQHTRQ`).
- Panorama mode displays institutional backbone only (Repo, Decision, Law, Analysis); correlation view requires explicit multi-repo selection and cross-node traversal (turns 5–6, graph mode refactor `01KQV804VBX0EG2G46HRQAW3TH`).

hits.title: Cortex performance audit + hook native shim (phase11x/12a)
hits.body:
Session triggered by user frustration: "consolidation doesn't work, memory cleanup needs brute force, data isn't relevant." Spawned 4 agents in parallel (3 researchers + architect) to audit consolidation pipeline, memory cleanup, retrieval relevance, and architecture—documented in `docs/analysis/rework/` (5 files, 1142 lines) and `docs/analysis/opencode-adapter/` (4 files). This identified 80% structural debt vs 20% patches, but focused work proceeded on immediate bottlenecks.

**Phase 11x (cortex-hook native shim):** Profiled hook latency on Windows to ~730ms per hook; root cause: PowerShell cold-start (545ms floor), not daemon. Implemented native Rust binary `cortex-hook` (~280 lines) to replace per-event `.sh`/`.ps1` shims, rewired `install.rs` to invoke the bin, added criterion benchmark harness (`hook_cold_start.rs`), daemon-side hook logging (`hook_log.rs`), and CI workflow `hook-cold-start.yml`. All tests pass; clippy clean; 4 commits.

**Phase 12a (consolidator publish fallback):** Added structured `tracing::error!` logging to all failure paths in `publish_consolidation()`, implemented JSONL fallback append-with-rotation (100MB threshold, 7 rotations kept) when ingestion POST fails, added `cortex-ops consolidations-replay --from <jsonl>` to replay from the fallback file. Updated CHANGELOG. 3 commits.

**Branch state:** 16 commits ahead of origin; working tree clean. Phase 11v (MCP fine-grained search) started but not implemented.

- **Hook latency root cause**: Windows PowerShell cold-start dominates (545ms/invocation) vs. daemon RPC (~90ms). Native cortex-hook binary avoids repeated pwsh invocation but cannot reduce the floor without moving to a compiled entry point or persistent runner (decision: native bin is the practical win at ~51ms startup, ~200ms total vs ~730ms/hook before).
- **Consolidator resilience**: Publish failures now roll over to JSONL file (`~/.cortex/consolidations-fallback.jsonl`) with 100MB rotation + operator replay tool (`cortex-ops consolidations-replay`), preventing silent data loss during ingestion pod restarts or network issues.
- **Rework analysis surfaced asymmetric decay**: Audit revealed consolidation and cleanup pipelines have accumulated structural debt (schema rewrite needed, pre-thinking truncation + relevance scoring are orthogonal issues), but OpenCode adapter is a pure encapsulation task (ready for phase11w). Dashboard consolidations view ships now; deeper rework deferred to phase16a.

hits.title: Consolidation tier closure (pruner → forget → graph fix)
hits.body:
Shipped three interconnected phases that close the consolidation workflow: **phase11o** (tier-demotion pruner with nightly cron), **phase11p** (consolidator live read path + HDBSCAN topic clustering), and **phase11t** (cortex_forget MCP tool + /v1/admin/forget endpoint). Alongside, debugged and fixed a CPU spike in cortex-api (corrupted parquet in archive_loader loop) and a critical Nexus 2.2.0 upgrade that exposed a volume persistence bug in docker-compose; re-bootstrapped the graph after fixing the mount to cortex, expert, lexum, vectorizersync, synap repos.

**Key files**: `crates/cortex-workers/src/pruner/` (5 modules, 1.2kL), `crates/cortex-workers/src/consolidator/source/` (3 modules, 900L), `crates/cortex-api/src/admin_forget.rs` (400L), `crates/cortex-mcp-server/src/tools.rs` (ForgetTool, 150L). Dependencies added: `hdbscan = "0.10"`. **Commit d186be3**: 55 files, 5811 insertions, 671 deletions. All tests passing, MCP server validated via cortex_pre_thinking and cortex_query intents.

**Infrastructure readiness**: Cortex backend coverage now 84/135 (62%) Vectorizer collections after full re-bootstrap. Nexus CPU issue resolved (2.1.0→2.2.0: 100%→4%). Graph dashboard live again post-bootstrap.

- HDBSCAN `min_samples=1` is required when `min_cluster_size` is at the floor (small datasets); without it, tight clusters become noise and the algorithm produces an empty result. Learned after 2+ failed iterations in topic.rs unit tests.
- Multi-phase task ordering (11o→11j→11p→11t) is structural, not stylistic — phase11j blocked until 11o shipped (pruner module), 11p shipped (consolidator), 11t shipped (forget endpoint). Respecting the DAG prevented costly re-sequencing.
- Silent container data loss: docker-compose `nexus-data:/data` should mount to `/app/data` inside the container, not `/data`. The mismatch persisted through multiple sessions until the Nexus 2.2.0 upgrade exposed it. Always verify volume WORKDIR post-major-upgrade.

hits.title: GUI refactor + security patch: move Retention into Health, redact leaked credent
hits.body:
Session completed two independent tasks in sequence: (1) **GUI refactoring** — moved the Retention view into Health screen and removed from sidebar menu. Modified `Retention.tsx` to use fragment + `health-section` CSS classes, removed retention from `Sidebar.tsx` ViewId type and menu, removed imports/case handlers in `App.tsx`. Type-checked and ran tests (14 pass). Committed as `e4bc184`. (2) **Security fix** — user discovered credentials in `scripts/graph/graph_correlate.cypher` (commit 1ec6a8a): 6× PyPI token, 3× NuGet API key, 1× Vectorizer JWT secret, all inside `text_excerpt` of `Cor_Turn` nodes. Root cause was that `graph_correlate.py` generator did not redact secrets from transcript prose before export. Added pattern-based redaction covering PyPI, NuGet, GitHub PAT, OpenAI, Anthropic, AWS, Google, Slack, HuggingFace, JWT, PEM, [REDACTED:bearer_token] Updated `.gitignore` to ignore `*.cypher`, used `git rm --cached` to untrack the leaked dump. Committed as `8debc3b`.

Both commits follow conventional format. GUI refactoring ran type-check multiple times and verified all tests pass before commit. Security patterns catch the most common shapes of credentials in prose ("token <X>", "api_key=<X>", "password: <X>").

- Redaction belongs in the generator, not at ingestion — transcript prose will inevitably contain pasted credentials; mask them before export rather than trying to prevent them from entering.
- Credential patterns are shaped by prose context — literal strings in user messages need looser regex than JSON payloads; the solution uses word boundaries and entropy checks, not just token prefixes.
- Graph dumps are untracked; they circulate in chat/email but are already in git history — after redaction fix, old dumps stay visible until force-purge (user kept file on disk but untracked it, allowing future runs to overwrite).

hits.title: Dashboard detail endpoints: add Analysis detail, fix truncation
hits.body:
## Problem
Dashboard UI showed incomplete data for Decisions and Analyses. The list endpoints clipped fields (600 char `rationale` / `verdict`) but the GUI's detail drawers had nowhere to fetch full content.

## Findings
- **Decisions**: list truncates `rationale` at 600 chars in `dashboard.rs:1048–1049`; detail endpoint existed but GUI wasn't wired to use it
- **Analyses**: no detail endpoint existed at all; list showed clipped `verdict` with no way to fetch full content

## Solution
1. **Backend** (`crates/cortex-api/src/dashboard.rs`): Added `AnalysisDetail` struct and `analysis_detail` handler (mirrors `decision_detail` pattern). Refactored row building into `build_analysis_row` helper to unclip body.
2. **Frontend** (`gui/src/lib/api.ts`): Added `AnalysisDetail` type and wired `analysisDetail()` endpoint call.
3. **Component** (`gui/src/views/Analysis.tsx`): Updated detail drawer to call the new endpoint instead of trying to render clipped list data.

## Verification
- `cargo check -p cortex-api` ✓
- `cargo build -p cortex-api --bin cortex-api` ✓  
- TypeScript type-check ✓

Build successful. Changes landed.

- Detail endpoints must return unclipped data; list endpoints truncate for table density — mirror the Decision detail pattern for Analyses
- Asymmetric API patterns (Decision has detail endpoint, Analysis doesn't) break component reuse; enforce symmetry when adding new dashboard items
- Clipping at API level (600 char limits) should be a list-only behavior, never leak into detail responses

hits.title: 10 retention/fulltext subsystem tasks archived (phase11x, phase12a-g) — 150+ ite
hits.body:
Session swept through a 7-task sequence consolidating the retention, fulltext (Meili), and consolidator subsystems. Archived: **phase11v** (2 tasks: MCP search + retention daemon recovery); **phase11x** (cortex-hook native shim with 14× Windows speedup baseline); **phase12a-g** (metrics, archive purge, schema definitions, vocabulary, audit tooling).

Key outputs: (1) new modules in cortex-storage (`archive_purge.rs`), cortex-workers (`consolidator/metrics.rs`, `fulltext/audit.rs`), cortex-core (`vocab.rs`); (2) JSON schemas for `knowledge` and `learning` event kinds; (3) Meili index settings for consolidations + topic-cards; (4) CLI subcommands `cortex-ops retention-archive-purge`, `cortex-ops meili-audit`, `cortex-ops meili-reindex`; (5) ADR-009 documenting cypher-gate default posture. Tests: 40+ new unit/integration tests, all green. Performance: Windows cortex-hook shim reduced hook latency from ~750ms (PowerShell) to ~52ms (native binary).

Session ended blocked on **phase13a** (sweep trait refactor) due to GitHub OAuth token missing `workflow` scope (caused by phase11x creating `.github/workflows/hook-cold-start.yml`). Handoff written; ready to resume in next session.

- **Cross-cutting concern consolidation pays off**: `is_live_partial_frame` (live frame guard used in both archive purge and admin forget) was successfully moved to `cortex_storage` as a public re-export. This unified the logic across two subsystems and enabled phase12b/c to reference a single source of truth, avoiding divergence.
- **Schema-first architecture gates downstream tooling**: Phase12d (knowledge + learning schemas) and phase12e (vocabulary) were implemented *before* the audit tool (phase12g). This enforced correctness early; when phase12g audits arrived, they found valid, validated event kinds waiting instead of discovering incomplete schemas during implementation.
- **CLI scope inflation requires explicit OAuth refresh**: The cortex-hook integration (phase11x §6.4) added GitHub Actions workflows, which push to `.github/workflows/`. Standard GitHub OAuth tokens lack `workflow` scope by default. Subsequent pushes fail silently; the fix (`gh auth refresh -s workflow`) is non-obvious. Future multi-service contributions should call this out early.

hits.title: Case-sensitivity repo deduplication + UI cleanup (dashboard.rs + 5 views)
hits.body:
Session fixed case-sensitivity duplication in repo aggregation and filtering across the API and GUI. User reported repos appearing as both `cortex` and `Cortex` in the dashboard sidebar.

**Root cause & API fix**: Added `normalize_repo()` helper in `crates/cortex-api/src/dashboard.rs:128` to lowercase all repo identifiers server-side. Applied normalization to overview aggregation (`line 218`), repo counting, and repo filter logic. Built and deployed cortex-api; dashboard confirmed returning deduplicated lowercase repos.

**GUI dropdown fixes**: Applied `.toLowerCase()` to repo option deduplication in 5 views (`Analysis.tsx`, `Decisions.tsx`, `Tasks.tsx`, `Handoffs.tsx`, `Conversations.tsx`) to handle case-insensitive filter comparisons. Fixed blank/white select dropdown styling by adding `color-scheme: dark;` to `gui/src/styles.css:1`.

**Card cleanup**: Removed unused 24h "Classifier spend" and 7d "Violations" cards from `gui/src/views/Timeline.tsx` + orphaned props (`violationsDaily`, `classifierCost`, `sessionsQ` query). All changes type-checked and compiled successfully.

- Case-sensitivity bugs require fixes at both boundaries: normalize at source (API response) to prevent duplicates, normalize at use (UI filters) to ensure consistent client-side matching.
- Dark-mode select dropdowns render white/invisible without explicit `color-scheme: dark;` in root CSS — a common oversight when copy-pasting light-mode stylesheets.
- Removing unused dashboard cards requires tracing props upstream through query definitions and component signatures; unused vars like `sessionsQ` are easy to miss and cause type errors.

hits.title: Consolidation live-read path + fine-grained backend search MCP tools
hits.body:
Session diagnosed why memory consolidation never ran in production: the consolidator binary was implemented (phase11j) but lacked integration into nightly runs. Consolidated work from the previous session (phase11p) that had already completed the live-source modules, envelope publication, and scheduler wiring but remained uncommitted. Added `ClaudeCliSummariser` subprocess wrapper (`crates/cortex-workers/src/consolidator/summariser_cli.rs`) to invoke `claude -p` instead of Anthropic API (per project's Claude Code CLI–only philosophy), wired envelope publishing to `/v1/events`, corrected stream type to `live`, and executed the first production nightly consolidation run—successfully consolidating ~617 sessions via subprocess Claude.

In parallel, implemented phase11v: three fine-grained backend search MCP tools (`/v1/search/keyword`, `/v1/search/vector`, `/v1/search/graph`) in `crates/cortex-api/src/search_proxy.rs` that expose raw access to Meili, Vectorizer, and Nexus backends, complementing the fused `cortex_query` tool. Updated tool registry and test assertions for 10-tool set. Dead end: initially investigated archive parquet structure and session enumeration before realizing the bottleneck was the missing publish/wiring layer, not data access.

**Files:** `crates/cortex-workers/src/consolidator/summariser_cli.rs` (new), `crates/cortex-workers/src/bin/cortex-consolidator.rs`, `crates/cortex-api/src/{search_proxy,http}.rs`, `crates/cortex-mcp-server/src/tools.rs`. Committed as `6816586`.

- Consolidation pipeline existed but was never invoked in production—missing envelope publish path and CLI wiring from consolidated source modules to binary; issue detected by running nightly consolidator for the first time against live archive.
- Project uses `claude` CLI subprocess exclusively; never passes ANTHROPIC_API_KEY to LLM inference code (verified in `CLAUDE.local.md` feedback). Must wrap LLM calls in CLI subprocess with `-p` (prompt mode) + `--output-format json` flags.
- Fine-grained backend search tools (keyword, vector, graph) expose raw per-backend query APIs as complement to fused `cortex_query`, enabling power-user direct access to Meili, Vectorizer, and Nexus without router fusion logic.

hits.title: Purged 58% of Cortex memory + shipped Consolidations dashboard view
hits.body:
Session investigated why `tool_call` envelopes (29,283 count) were not being purged by the scheduled `cortex-ops tool-call-digest` pipeline. Diagnosis revealed the `already_digested` flag was not cascading through the forget loop, preventing cleanup.

Implemented three fixes: (1) added `--age-days N` and `--min-bucket-size N` CLI overrides to `cortex-ops` ([cortex-ops.rs](crates/cortex-cli/src/bin/cortex-ops.rs), [digest.rs](crates/cortex-cli/src/bin/cortex-ops/digest.rs:327)) to bypass the 30-day retention policy for emergency cleanup; (2) patched the `already_digested` cascade logic ([digest.rs](crates/cortex-cli/src/bin/cortex-ops/digest.rs:525)) to mark digested buckets correctly; (3) ran parallel bulk `/v1/admin/forget` loops to directly purge events > 48h old, then manually removed 80 archive partitions.

Memory dropped 58% (40,869 → 17,058 events; tool_call 29,774 → 8,129). Also completed the Consolidations dashboard feature that surfaced cross-project consolidation envelopes (513 indexed via Meili). Shipped as single commit with cortex-ops + consolidations-endpoint + consolidations-view.

- Retention policy defaults (30d minimum for tool-call-digest) don't match operator emergency cleanup needs. Added CLI escape hatches, but suggest making thresholds configurable in TOML to avoid re-patching on each sweep.
- Dashboard lane state loads from archive on boot + periodic refresh; deletes don't trigger refresh automatically. Manual `/v1/admin/forget` worked but container restart was needed to see count changes — potential race in lane population.
- Bulk `/v1/admin/forget` is reliable (confirmed via Meili/Nexus delete markers) but processes 1 event/request. 30-parallel requests helped, but batch endpoint would be faster for >1000-event cleanups.

hits.title: Consolidated model audits into 32-task rework roadmap (phases 12–16)
hits.body:
Three independent model audits (GLM5.1, MinMax2.7, Opus5.7) converged on the same verdict: Cortex needs **medium rework, not rewrite**. Session consolidated their findings and created a comprehensive 32-task breakdown across 5 phases. Phase 12 (7 tasks) addresses tactical patches; Phase 13 (6 tasks) codifies trait abstractions (ADRs 9–11, 14, 16–17); Phase 14 (9 tasks) implements those traits; Phase 15 (6 tasks) handles bootstrap, graph mapping, and laws DSL; Phase 16 (4 tasks) adds adapter support (OpenCode, Cursor, Codex, Gemini). Task files were written to `.rulebook/tasks/phase12*–16*/proposal.md` and `tasks.md`. Three existing tasks (phase11v retention recovery marked complete retroactively; phase11v fine-grained search and phase11w opencode adapter marked blocked pending trait definitions). All new tasks validated and integrated into Rulebook task hierarchy.

- Multiple independent audits produce high-confidence diagnosis — GLM5.1, MinMax2.7, and Opus5.7 all identified same root issues (missing schemas, cron TOCTOU, adapter panics, consolidator fallback), validating the audit findings from `docs/analysis/rework/`.
- Task decomposition mirrored audit structure: phases 12–13 are prerequisites (tactical patches + trait definitions), phases 14–16 are dependent work (implementations + adapters). This sequencing enforces LSP dependency order.
- Write operation issues were worked around by reading skeleton templates and rewriting proposal/tasks files in sequence — indicates Rulebook task creation succeeded but post-creation file operations had transient issues.

hits.title: Retention daemon recovery + tool-call memory digestion (phase11v–phase11w)
hits.body:
## Scope

Two-phase work spanning 14 days: (a) identified and fixed 6 independent gaps in the retention daemon that all surfaced as "every sweep says never"; (b) built tool-call digest summarizer to purge old tool-call envelopes and recover memory.

## Phase 11v — Retention Daemon Recovery

Dashboard reported 0 next_run dates for all retention sweeps. Investigation revealed **six unrelated failures**:

1. **Dashboard hardcoded `"never"`** — [crates/cortex-api/src/dashboard.rs:3639](crates/cortex-api/src/dashboard.rs#L3639-L3653) `retention_state()` ignored the actual `cron_jobs` DB table.
2. **Memory consolidate disabled in DB** — `C:\Users\Bolado\.cortex\metadata.sqlite` had `enabled=0` from earlier session, blocking Sunday 07:00 UTC sweep.
3. **Env var precedence inverted** — [crates/cortex-cli/src/bin/cortex-ops.rs:4609](crates/cortex-cli/src/bin/cortex-ops.rs#L4609) checked `CORTEX_EMBEDDER_VECTORIZER_URL` before `CORTEX_VECTORIZER_URL` (docker-compose exports the latter).
4. **Nexus container panicked** — cypher_load.py flood caused 400+ statement queue overflow, panicked workers.
5. **Scheduler seed_defaults bug** — `next_after()` cron helper didn't advance past exact time matches; DOW field accepted both `0` and `7` for Sunday causing ambiguity.
6. **Missing `sweep_bookkeeping` module** — each `cortex-ops <sweep>` command wasn't recording its outcome to `retention_sweeps` table.

All surfaced as single symptom: dashboard displaying `next_run: "never"` for all 9 scheduled sweeps. Fixes: (a) read DB live in dashboard, (b) re-enable memory_consolidate in DB, (c) flip env check order, (d) extend `ScheduledRun` type with `last_status` + `failure_streak`, (e) fix cron DOW normalization, (f) inject bookkeeping into all 8 sweep commands via `sweep_bookkeeping.rs` helper.

## Phase 11w — Tool-Call Digest Summarizer

Memory index had ~40K tool_call envelopes bloating `/root/.claude/projects/*/memory`. Built summarization pipeline: bucketize by `(repo, year-week, tool_name)`, apply Claude to summarize bucket, emit `consolidation` envelope (replaces originals), delete via `/v1/admin/forget`. New modules: [crates/cortex-workers/src/retention/tool_call_digest.rs](crates/cortex-workers/src/retention/tool_call_digest.rs) (summarizer), [crates/cortex-cli/src/bin/cortex-ops/tool_call_digest_live.rs](crates/cortex-cli/src/bin/cortex-ops/tool_call_digest_live.rs) (live deletion backend), [crates/cortex-api/src/admin_list_events.rs](crates/cortex-api/src/admin_list_events.rs) (event enumeration endpoint for cron orchestrator). Added to scheduler: `tool-call-digest --apply --purge-originals` runs Wed 03:00 UTC on-demand.

## Key Files

- `scripts/graph_correlate.py` (new): cross-project correlation analyzer → Cypher dump
- `scripts/cypher_load.py` (new): parallel Cypher statement loader with backoff
- `docker-compose.yml`: added `CORTEX_VECTORIZER_USER` + host mount for Claude projects
- `.rulebook/tasks/phase11v_retention-daemon-recovery/`: task with 8 sections, all completed


- Six independent subsystem failures (dashboard, DB state, env vars, cron math, bookkeeping, Nexus overload) all manifested as single user-visible symptom ("all sweeps say never"). Diagnosis required tracing from dashboard → DB → logs → scheduler → each sweep impl.
- Retention daemon requires both enumeration API (`/v1/admin/list-events`) and deletion API (`/v1/admin/forget`) to be live for background cron jobs to work; enumerator + orchestrator are siblings, not sequential.
- Tool-call memory bloat solved by scheduled summarization (Wed 03:00 UTC): bucketize by repo+week+tool, compress 100 tool_calls → 1 consolidation envelope, purge originals via admin API. Drops memory index from 40K docs to ~100 weekly summaries.

hits.title: Parallel consolidation of 18 HiveLLM projects into structured knowledge bases
hits.body:
User initiated a parallel knowledge-capture task: consolidate every HiveLLM project (Cortex, Vectorizer, Nexus, Synap, Expert, Lexum, Rulebook, Tml, Umicp, HiveGPU, HivehubCloud, Transmutation, TransmutationLite, VectorizerSync, CompressionPrompt, TmlTextmate, TmlDocs, Assets) into a standardized markdown KB format for future Cortex ingestion.

Approach: Dispatched parallel researchers via Agent tool for each project (turns starting 01KQV0RJTK05, 01KQV0V1NC4Z6ZW1MS431B1E0P, 01KQV0V4Y8WHE5DWNX8E59Z39G, etc.). Each project received a 9-file template:
- 01: overview (purpose, role, status)
- 02: architecture (layering, components)
- 03: public-surface (APIs, CLIs, endpoints)
- 04: data-and-storage (schemas, state ownership)
- 05: integrations (HiveLLM ecosystem relationships)
- 06: decisions-and-rationale (architectural choices)
- 07: operational (deployment, runtime, Docker)
- 08: cortex-relevance (what Cortex should ingest)
- 09: open-questions (gaps, unknowns)
- README.md per-project index

Output: 166 markdown files across `docs/consolidation/<Project>/`, landing in commit `7f1b7fb` (`docs(consolidation): per-project KB snapshot for 18 Hive repos`). This consolidation ran in parallel with the active task (phase14c) without interference.

- Parallel Agent dispatch + per-project researchers scaled linearly: 18 agents spawned at once (vs. sequential) completed in one session despite full-codebase reads. Parallelism required no coordination; each agent's output was independent (Write tool to separate project dirs).
- 9-section template proved sufficient for comprehensive coverage: consistency across 18 diverse projects (language ecosystems: Rust, TypeScript, Python, Tml) suggests the granularity (overview→decisions→gaps) maps well to the information needs of systems integration work.
- Knowledge consolidation successfully decoupled from task execution: ran in parallel to phase14c ("active task") without blocking; commit isolated to docs/ tree, leaving cortex-api, docker-compose, gui untouched—clean separation of exploratory KB work from implementation work.

hits.title: Strategic Cortex rework analysis — second opinion + validation

- Explored consolidator daemon, pruner/retention, and quality-gate patterns systematically; confirmed no major architectural debt or unhandled edge cases in current state

hits.title: Phase 11x cortex-hook native shim + Phase 12a consolidator resilience
hits.body:
Session started with user frustration over consolidation, memory cleanup, and retrieval relevance ("consolidation doesn't work, data doesn't result in anything relevant"). Spawned 4 parallel auditors (researchers + architect) to diagnose; captured findings in `docs/analysis/rework/` and discovered 80% structural debt, not quick fixes.

Pivoted to performance bottleneck investigation after user asked why responses were slow. Profiled hooks and identified pwsh cold-start (~545ms per invocation) as the floor. This led to **phase11x**: replaced per-event shell shims (`.ps1`/`.sh`) with native Rust binary `cortex-hook` (~51ms) + daemon-side hook_log rotation. Implemented criterion benchmark + CI gate (`hook-cold-start.yml`) to prevent future regressions. 4 commits; 2010/2010 tests passing.

**Phase 12a** (consolidator publish resilience): added structured failure logging + JSONL fallback file at `~/.cortex/consolidations-fallback.jsonl` with 100MB rotation + `cortex-ops consolidations-replay` recovery tool. 3 commits. Incomplete: phase11x §5 (env var bootstrap on operator pod) + §7.1–7.3 (docs/learnings/ADR) pending external state.

Started phase11v (MCP fine-grained backend search) but did not implement — session context saturation triggered handoff planning.

- Windows hook latency is bound by PowerShell cold-start (~545ms), not daemon IPC. Native binary replacement cuts per-hook overhead from 730ms to 51ms (14× improvement). Source: 01KQYHE3V44C2QVH6S6X456MYJ profiling + benches/baseline-2026-05-06.txt.
- Consolidator publish failures went silent → added structured logs + JSONL fallback with rotation. Operator can now replay failed envelopes via `cortex-ops consolidations-replay --from ~/.cortex/consolidations-fallback.jsonl`. Source: commits 2373c28 (logs), 7b57f2b (rotation).
- User frustration driver was not bugs but debt architecture (80/20 split). Rework analysis uncovered that consolidation, cleanup, relevance are entangled at the schema/indexing layer, not isolated problems. Documented in docs/analysis/rework/04-architecture.md as a decision point for rewrite vs. patch strategy. Source: 01KQXF7RBTD3YGXCVM0ZJB7W2M parallel audits.

hits.title: Consolidation pruning pipeline: phases 11o/p/t + infrastructure recovery
hits.body:
Implemented three coordinated phases completing the consolidation tier's prune-then-serve architecture. **Phase11o** (`crates/cortex-workers/src/pruner/`) adds nightly hard-purge and tier-demotion sweeps (vectorizer & Meili), integrated with the retention daemon. **Phase11p** (`crates/cortex-workers/src/consolidator/source/`) provides live-read-path sources (session, topic, decision-trace) powered by HDBSCAN clustering and archive-side envelope scanning helpers in `cortex-api/src/archive_loader.rs`. **Phase11t** (`crates/cortex-api/src/admin_forget.rs` + MCP `ForgetTool`) exposes the purge backend over HTTP and via MCP.

Infrastructure work consumed ~40% of effort: (1) cortex-api running archive_loader every 30s on corrupt parquet, quarantined bad file to cut 50% CPU; (2) cortex-nexus 2.1.0 burning 100% CPU, upgraded to 2.2.0 (from Nexus repo commit 24035285) reducing to 3–4%; (3) docker-compose volume mount pointed to wrong path, fixed to `nexus-data:/app/data`. Added `hdbscan = "0.10"` as workspace dependency. All three phases archived after passing unit + integration tests; final commit `d186be3` bundles 55 files, 5811 insertions, 671 deletions.

- HDBSCAN topic clustering requires `min_samples=1` at `min_cluster_size` floor to avoid under-clustering tight envelope groups (observed in phase11p unit tests; resolved by inspecting hdbscan crate source and adjusting HyperParams).
- Infrastructure diagnostics must resolve CPU and I/O issues before feature work—quarantining corrupt archive files and upgrading Nexus image removed blocking 100%+ CPU load that would have masked consolidation logic bugs.
- Three-phase decomposition (pruner backend → consolidator live-read → MCP exposure) successfully decoupled storage operations, orchestration logic, and API surface, enabling independent testing and future iteration.

hits.title: Phase11v retention daemon + split large Rust files into modular architecture
hits.body:
Consolidated phase11v retention daemon recovery (§5 tail) and implemented missing live backends for turn/tool-call digest. Split two large files — `dashboard.rs` (5005→415 lines) and `cortex-ops.rs` (4962→1131 lines) — into per-topic submodules across 17+16 files respectively. Reorganized `/scripts/` from flat 32-file layout into thematic subdirectories (doctor, sweeps, graph, probes, setup).

During testing, surfaced and fixed five edge-case bugs in digest/purge pipeline: schema validation for envelope persistence (`cortex-core/schemas/`), Vectorizer JWT wiring in `/v1/admin/forget` cascade, ULID timestamp recovery when archive events carry `ts=0/occurred_at=1970`, metadata-DB resolution respecting `CORTEX_HOME` env var, and zstd frame tolerance in live archive rewriter for partial frames. Ran full drain of tool_call + turn digests to completion (50k+ records).

**Key files**: `crates/cortex-api/src/dashboard/*.rs` (17 submodules); `crates/cortex-cli/src/bin/cortex-ops/*.rs` (16 submodules); `crates/cortex-api/src/admin_forget.rs` (zstd frame fix); `crates/cortex-api/src/http.rs` (Vectorizer auth); `crates/cortex-cli/src/bin/cortex-ops/helpers.rs` (CORTEX_HOME resolution). **16 commits** on `main`, branch ahead of origin by 16.

- Splitting large files (>4k lines) by topic—not by size—improves navigation and team onboarding. Both `dashboard.rs` and `cortex-ops.rs` became immediately more discoverable; per-repo index naming in Meili (`cortex-<repo>-turns`) and index grain (consolidator running topic-keyed nightly) are now aligned with split structure.
- Admin purge operations (`/v1/admin/forget` cascade) need three defensive layers: schema validation (envelope must pass `memory.schema.json`), timestamp recovery from ULID when events carry `ts=0` from boot-time archive load, and zstd frame tolerance since live archive files may be written incompletely during shutdown—normal ingestion never hits these edge cases.
- Metadata database resolution (`cortex-ops schedule`, `memory-consolidate`) must respect `CORTEX_HOME` env var consistently across all subcommands, not just discovery. Container deployments fail silently when `helpers.rs::resolve_metadata_db()` defaults to user home instead of `/var/lib/cortex/` mount.

hits.title: Phase 11–12 tail: Cortex hook shim + consolidation suite (7 tasks)
hits.body:
Session closed 7 rulebook tasks across phases 11–12, completing critical infrastructure work.

**Phase 11 tail**: Finalized `phase11x_cortex-hook-native-shim` (32/32 items), achieving ~14× speedup over PowerShell shim on Windows (51–55ms p50). Added `.github/workflows/hook-cold-start.yml` for CI smoke tests.

**Phase 12 consolidation** (a–g): Unified retention/archival/schema/Meili infrastructure across 8+ crates:
- **12a**: `cortex_consolidator_publish_failures_total{reason}` Prometheus counter in `cortex-workers/src/consolidator/metrics.rs`
- **12b**: Parquet archive purge in `cortex-storage/src/archive_purge.rs` + `cortex-ops retention-archive-purge` CLI; cron seed bumped to 11 jobs
- **12c**: `is_live_partial_frame` consolidated into `cortex_storage`; `tool_call_digest` post-flip defaults reconciled
- **12d**: JSON schemas for `knowledge` and `learning` events; Meili index settings for `consolidations` and `topic_cards`; `cortex-ops doctor-meili-indexes` command
- **12e**: `KIND_IDS` vocabulary complete (IDs 9–12); compile-time enum guard
- **12f**: `record_cron_run` TOCTOU race fixed (atomic single-UPDATE statement)
- **12g**: `cortex-ops meili-audit` + `cortex-workers/src/fulltext/audit.rs` audit module

All tasks: passed `cargo check`/`test`/`clippy` gates, CHANGELOG updated, archived via rulebook MCP. Final push blocked on GitHub OAuth: token lacks `workflow` scope for CI files added in phase11x §6.4. Fix: `gh auth refresh -s workflow && git push`.

- Phase 12 is tightly coupled: task order is critical. Schema registration (12d, 12e) precedes audit/archival (12g, 12b); shared guards (12c) precede consumers. Reordering breaks dependencies.
- Real Windows smoke testing matters more than synthetic benchmarks. Phase11x §5.1 captured native shim p50 at 51–55ms on developer box—this baseline informs future optimization targets.
- GitHub OAuth scopes are environment state, not code. When pushing CI workflows, refresh the token scope via `gh auth refresh -s workflow`. Document in future session handoffs.

hits.title: Fix case-sensitivity repo duplication across API and GUI layers
hits.body:
Session fixed a case-sensitivity bug where repositories appeared deduplicated in API but duplicated in GUI (e.g., `cortex` and `Cortex` shown separately). The fix spanned two layers:

**Backend (API)**: Modified `crates/cortex-api/src/dashboard.rs` to add a `normalize_repo()` helper that lowercases all repo identifiers at the source. Updated 6+ filter/comparison points: overview aggregation, per-kind breakdown, lane-hit repo handling, and repo-set filtering. Validated with `cargo check` + release build + HTTP healthcheck.

**Frontend (GUI)**: Updated repo dropdown dedup logic in 5 view components (`Analysis.tsx`, `Decisions.tsx`, `Tasks.tsx`, `Handoffs.tsx`, `Conversations.tsx`) to call `.toLowerCase()` when building option lists and filtering. Also removed two unused dashboard cards (`Classifier spend · 24h`, `Violations · 7d`) from `Timeline.tsx` and fixed dropdown styling by adding `color-scheme` to `styles.css`.

Verified: typecheck clean, API returns lowercase repos, sidebar shows single deduplicated entries, dropdown filters work case-insensitively.

- Case-sensitivity bugs that span frontend + backend must be normalized at the **authoritative source** (API layer) first, then cascaded to frontends—normalize at creation time (dedup sets, option lists), not filter time.
- When fixing repo comparisons across multiple components, use a **consistent normalization strategy** (`.toLowerCase()`) at every compare point to avoid future divergence; helper functions at the API level reduce frontend repetition.
- Dropdown styling can silently fail if base CSS variables (`color-scheme`) are missing—test the full visual output (not just typecheck) after filter refactors.

hits.title: Memory consolidation live + fine-grained backend search (phase11p tail + phase11
hits.body:
Session tackled two major gaps: **phase11p (consolidator live read path)** was implemented months ago but never executed in production, and **phase11v (MCP fine-grained backend search)** needed per-backend query access.

**Phase11p execution** (commits d186be3 + 3b4d740): Discovered that consolidator binary + live session readers + publishing logic were already coded in archive (2026-05-05-phase11p). Rebuilt release binary, integrated with `claude -p` CLI for session summarization, wired envelope publishing to `/v1/events` endpoint, and executed full corpus consolidation (`nightly --all`). Now processing 617 archived sessions one-at-a-time via Claude CLI subprocess. Key implementation: `ClaudeCliSummariser` spawns `claude -p -` per session, streams summary through orchestrator, publishes as Envelope to ingest with stream="live" + tool="cortex-cli".

**Phase11v implementation** (commit 6816586): Added three new HTTP search proxies (`crates/cortex-api/src/search_proxy.rs`) and wired to MCP tools: `POST /v1/search/keyword` (Meili passthrough), `/v1/search/vector` (raw Vectorizer search), `/v1/search/graph` (Nexus CyPHER queries). User wanted fine-grained access to individual backends instead of only fused `cortex_query`. Registered 3 new tools in MCP server (total 7→10 tools). All endpoints tested, mocked vector/graph handlers pending live Vectorizer API availability.

- **Implementation debt from archive**: Phase11p was coded + tested but archived without live execution—architectural work finished but production integration deferred. Periodic "did we actually run this" audits catch such gaps before they accumulate. Trigger: check if major completed tasks have corresponding prod usage / cron jobs / running processes.
- **User intent forced execution**: Session pivoted from task-structure work to immediate binary execution when user said "stop explaining, consolidate". The work was done; it just needed to *run*. Teaches: sometimes finishing is about removing blocking ops (binary build, subprocess integration, publish wiring) not more code.
- **Proxy-first backend access**: Fine-grained search via three simple `/v1/search/{keyword,vector,graph}` endpoints proved better than a single fused query. Each backend (Meili, Vectorizer, Nexus) has distinct semantics; proxy layers let callers compose, filter, or drill-down per backend without abstraction loss.

hits.title: Fixed missing `/v1/dashboard/analyses/{id}` endpoint — stale Docker container
hits.body:
Session investigated a 404 error when accessing the analysis detail endpoint (`/v1/dashboard/analyses/{id}`). Code review showed the route was correctly implemented in `dashboard.rs` (commit d186be3), and the frontend (`Analysis.tsx`) was calling it properly. However, curl testing revealed the endpoint returned 404 while the list endpoint (`/v1/dashboard/analyses`) worked fine. Root cause: the `cortex-api` Docker container had been running for 2 days on a stale image built before the route was added. Rebuilt the container image and restarted the service; endpoint immediately became available. This was a deployment state issue, not a code defect — the implementation was correct, the server binary was out of date.

- Stale container images can mask code changes. When a new route is added to source but returns 404 at runtime, verify the container was rebuilt and restarted after the code change.
- Live endpoint testing (curl) caught the symptom early (404 vs 200 for list endpoint) and ruled out frontend bugs before diving into code analysis.
- Docker image staleness is transparent to local code review — symptom only appears when testing against the running service, not via `git log` or file reads.

hits.title: Phase13a/13b completion + consolidation system hardening + post-consolidation cl
hits.body:
Session completed phase13a (Sweep trait + 7 retention sweep wrappers, ADR-009) and phase13b (EnvelopeProducer trait + 4 producers, ADR-010), both archived. Discovered + fixed cron seed bug in `scheduler.rs:312` where `default_jobs()` registered consolidator with wrong command string; diagnosed via `cortex-ops schedule list` binary execution.

Investigated consolidation quality issue ("716 garbage"). Root cause: session producer rendering Turns with empty user/assistant content → no substance floor filtering. Implemented two gates: (1) `SessionInput::ensure_non_empty()` rejects all-empty-Turn envelopes upfront; (2) relevance gate checks summariser output for garbage marker `"## Garbage"` post-LLM. Increased title cap 80→200 chars, summary 2000→4000 bytes via `crates/cortex-core/src/events.rs` + schema.

Fixed `archive_loader::envelope_to_hit()` bug: consolidation `body_markdown` was not being stamped into hit's `text` field, breaking dashboard preview. Backfill on 59-session inventory: 33 published (56%), 18 relevance rejects (31%), 3 substance rejects (5%), garbage markers + oversize rejects (2%). Quality verified via sample inspection: tml codegen root-cause analysis, ar-v3 refactor, cortex/tml/nexus consolidations all substantive. Post-consolidation purge: 2530 source event_ids via `/v1/admin/forget` cascade (4 backends), 3383 successful, 2657 already-removed. Final state: 44 high-quality consolidations indexed + 2 test consolidations archived.

- **Session producer substance floor is critical**: Turns with empty user_message + empty assistant_message pollute the consolidation index. Filtering at envelope-level before summariser call saves LLM tokens (claude CLI) and prevents garbage indexing. Pair with post-model relevance gate (LLM must explicitly reject via marker string).
- **Double-gate consolidation acceptance achieves 56% signal rate**: Substance floor (content must exist) + relevance gate (summariser output validation) rejected 44% of candidates as low-signal; verified remainder (33 published) all have usable summaries. Tested on real code (1619–5005 line sessions); sample outputs are ready for grounding / pre-thinking context injection.
- **Container binary stale-state requires full rebuild + verification**: API changes (extras extraction, body_markdown stamping) did not propagate to docker container despite `docker-compose build` — only `--no-cache` rebuild + restart worked. Verified via `sha256sum` binary hash mismatch. Impacts any deployment where cached layers hide code changes; always force rebuild when semantics change.

hits.title: Consolidations dashboard endpoint + memory purge (40k→17k events)
hits.body:
## Session summary

Investigated and resolved severe memory bloat (40,869 events) in the Cortex dashboard. Root cause: tool_call records were accumulating without corresponding archive purge. Deleted 80 archival partitions >48h old, reducing footprint 17M→5M and event count 40k→17k.

In parallel, implemented `/v1/dashboard/consolidations` endpoint to surface Consolidation envelopes (cross-repo session/topic/decision summaries) instead of raw event noise. This is institutional memory from phase11j consolidation work.

**Files touched:**
- `crates/cortex-api/src/dashboard.rs` — added `consolidations` route, updated `symbol_to_kind` enum
- `crates/cortex-api/src/dashboard/consolidations.rs` — new module (Consolidation envelope surface)
- `crates/cortex-api/src/meili_loader.rs` — added consolidations lane + seeding logic
- `gui/src/views/Consolidations.tsx` — new React view (table + detail drawer)
- `gui/src/lib/api.ts` — added types `ConsolidationRow`, `ConsolidationDetail`
- `gui/src/App.tsx`, `gui/src/shell/Sidebar.tsx` — routing + menu integration
- `scripts/sweeps/bulk-forget-tool-calls.ps1` — age-days/min-bucket-size overrides for manual purge

**Endpoint now live:** 513 consolidation documents indexed, queryable at `GET /v1/dashboard/consolidations`.

**Dead end:** Initial attempt to fix dashboard count updates failed (count didn't reflect deleted events). Worked around by rebuilding dashboard lanes from archive on container restart.

- Archive partition purge happens asynchronously in `admin_forget`; dashboard lane seeding does not auto-refresh counts. Manual container restart clears stale lane cache (turn 01KQX8MWXGN).
- Consolidations are institutional knowledge artifacts (session digests, decision traces) stored separately from raw events. Exposing them at the dashboard layer surfaces analysis results without event noise bloat (turns 01KQX9N1Z, 01KQX9SSP2S3).
- PowerShell bulk-forget loop needs explicit `confirmation_token` header to actually purge; dry-run defaults to false but state still lives in archive until partition rewrite (turn 01KQX8TX5DD).

hits.title: Fix cortex-config coverage to 90%+ and repair cascading build errors from LaneHi
hits.body:
Session fixed widespread build breakage caused by a missing `overlay` field in the `LaneHit` struct, which rippled across cortex-api, cortex-workers, cortex-cli, and cortex-mcp-server test code. The agent systematically added `overlay: Default::default()` to all `LaneHit` constructor sites in test files (cortex-api/tests/http.rs, decision_lookup_it.rs, governance_global_index_it.rs, law_check_it.rs, nexus_graph_lane.rs). It also fixed function call signatures in cortex-api/src/main.rs to stop passing stale arguments (build_nexus_client(), api_keys_db_path(), resolve_metadata_db_path()).

Secondary fixes included updating consolidator integration tests to use proper Cortex event envelope structure (`turn_envelope`, `tool_calls` arrays) instead of bare `user_message`/`assistant_message` JSON. Fixed `StubSummariser` implementations to return `RelevanceVerdict` results. Corrected date handling in cortex-cli log_rotate test to account for filesystem timestamp precision (test was failing because file age was being compared as whole days, but metadata precision caused rounding issues). Verified hook file sync between cortex-adapter-claude-code and cortex-plugin directories.

Workspace now builds and cortex-config reaches ~95%+ line coverage. All major test suites (consolidator, fulltext, api integ tests) passing.

- The `LaneHit::overlay: Overlay` field is a recent addition requiring systematic fixes across all test constructors—grep 'LaneHit {' in all crates/*/tests/*.rs to catch future regressions
- Consolidator tests require properly structured event envelopes (turn_envelope with SummariserResult containing RelevanceVerdict)—don't use bare JSON objects for turn/tool data in synthetic test sessions
- Date-based file rotation tests must account for filesystem timestamp precision; use `SystemTime::checked_sub()` or mock time boundaries rather than comparing age_days as integers
